movement_source: row 'Return on equity (ROE) (%) — Cash basis', column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 25 (cash basis) -> column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 (cash basis)
headline: CBA's cash ROE rose 50bpts to 14.0% in FY26 from 13.5% in FY25 (ev-1, ev-7, ev-16). The bank's only stated decomposition is narrative: ROE "increased 50 basis points to 14.0% with higher cash NPAT being partly offset by higher net assets" (ev-9). Cash NPAT from continuing operations rose $730m or 7% to $10,982m, driven by a 6% increase in operating income, a 6% increase in operating expenses and a $62m higher loan impairment expense (ev-10). Average net assets — the ROE denominator — rose from $75,710m to $78,238m (ev-5, ev-32), diluting the earnings lift. On a statutory basis ROE rose the same 50bpts, 13.4% to 13.9% (ev-1), with statutory NPAT up $778m or 8% (ev-14), so no material basis divergence. CBA publishes no quantified ROE walk; the earnings/equity split below is my arithmetic derivation from the cited endpoints and the stated earnings growth rate, not a bank disclosure.

drivers.narrative: Derived, not disclosed: 13.5% x 7.12% growth. CBA states ROE rose "with higher cash NPAT" (ev-9). Cash NPAT +$730m or 7% to $10,982m, from 6% operating income growth, 6% expense growth and $62m higher LIE (ev-10). NII +7% on 8%/$92bn AIEA growth, underlying NIM stable (ev-11).

drivers.bank_label: partly offset by higher net assets
drivers.columns: FY26 vs FY25 average net assets ($m)
drivers.narrative: Derived as total delta minus earnings effect, not disclosed. CBA says the NPAT lift was "partly offset by higher net assets" (ev-9). Average net assets rose $75,710m to $78,238m (ev-5, ev-32). Retained profits built $43,974m to $46,601m (ev-22); no buy-back in FY26 (ev-30) and the DRP was satisfied by on-market purchase (ev-20). CBA attributed FY25's 10bpt ROE fall to "growth in retained profits" (ev-26).

notable_items: FY26 operating expenses exclude restructuring and notable items: provisions for settlement of legal proceedings in NZ, an additional goodwill payment from ASIC's Better Banking review, and domestic customer remediation; FY25 related to domestic and NZ customer remediation and a Bankwest restructuring provision (ev-10 footnote context, not separately cited)
Cash-to-statutory bridge FY26: (Loss)/gain on acquisition, disposal, closure and demerger of businesses -$62m and Hedging and IFRS volatility -$54m

disagreements.topic: Closing vs average shareholders' equity direction
values: Closing equity $78,776m (Jun 25) to $78,704m (Jun 26) — broadly flat/slightly down
disagreements.explanation: The ROE denominator is average shareholders' equity (ev-5, ev-32), not the closing balance. Closing equity is flat only because reserves swung from +$1,242m to -$1,428m (ev-28, ev-29), a negative OCI movement concentrated late in the period; retained profits rose $2,627m. The average basis is the correct one for attributing the ROE movement.

limitations: CBA publishes NO quantified ROE walk or bridge chart for FY26 vs FY25 in any document searched. The earnings/equity split is my own arithmetic derivation (earnings_effect = prior ROE x earnings growth; equity_effect = residual), so its framing is not the bank's. The bank's own statement is qualitative only: 'higher cash NPAT being partly offset by higher net assets' (ev-9).

The earnings growth rate used is the stated 7% / $730m on continuing operations (ev-10); using unrounded endpoints ($10,982m/$75,710m) would give an earnings effect of roughly +1.0ppt and a correspondingly larger equity drag. The 0.96/-0.46 split is therefore sensitive to rounding in the printed 13.5% and 7% figures.
ROE endpoints are on a continuing operations basis; the KPI table prints identical 14.0%/13.5% cash figures including discontinued operations (ev-1), so this does not affect the movement.

The equity_effect direction is supported by cited reasoning (retained-earnings build, no FY26 buy-back, DRP satisfied on-market) but the bank does not quantify how much of the average-equity increase came from each source.

CBA's underlying NIM is described as 'stable' excluding liquid assets while reported NIM fell 3bpts to 2.05% (ev-11, ev-18); the earnings driver is therefore a volume-led rather than margin-led story, and the walk-level bar for this does not exist.
The FY26 presentation's capital chart (p32) is a Dec 25 to Jun 26 CET1 walk — a different comparison and a different metric — so none of its bars were used as contributions.

evidence_records.quote: CBA delivered a strong FY26 result. Cash net profit after tax increased 7% to $11bn, pre-provision profit increased 6% to $16.5bn and return on equity rose to 14.0%.

The full year dividend payout ratio is 77% of cash NPAT, within our target payout range of 70-80%. The Dividend Reinvestment Plan continues to be offered to shareholders and for this period is expected to be satisfied through the on-market purchase of shares.

Net profit after tax (NPAT) was supported by lending volume growth in our core businesses, with underlying net interest margin broadly stable. This was partly offset by higher operating expenses primarily due to inflation and technology investments, and a higher loan impairment expense due to portfolio growth and increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty.
